Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the CloudForge Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question during the Q&A, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity for everyone to ask a question. Please be advised that today's call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to CloudForge's Q3 FY2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Sarah Chen, CEO; Mike Patel, CFO; Dr. Lena Novak, CTO; Jordan Lee, Chief Revenue Officer; Taylor Kim, Chief Product Officer; and Riley Thompson, Chief Marketing Officer.

Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements. Actual results may differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. I'm pleased to report on CloudForge's performance for Q3 FY2024. We achieved significant milestones this quarter, driven by strong demand for our ForgeAI platform and continued execution of our strategic initiatives.

Our focus this quarter was on seven key areas: ARR growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, gross margin expansion, sales efficiency improvements, free cash flow generation, product roadmap advancements, key assumptions underlying our guidance, and next-quarter ARR outlook.

These efforts have positioned us for sustained momentum as we navigate a dynamic macro environment. We are confident in our ability to continue this momentum and deliver long-term value to our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Patel to discuss the financials in more detail.

Mike Patel:
Thank you, Sarah. As Sarah mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $115 million, representing a 28% increase year-over-year. Our GAAP gross margin was 78.5%, and non-GAAP operating income was $35 million.

We continue to invest in research and development to drive innovation and expand our product offerings. Our cash position remains strong at $450 million, providing us with the flexibility to pursue strategic acquisitions and other growth opportunities.

We are updating our full-year guidance to reflect our strong performance in the first three quarters. We now expect FY2024 revenue to be in the range of $460 million to $475 million, with ARR at the midpoint of $1.85 billion.

Turning first to our top-line momentum, I'm pleased to report that we delivered another quarter of robust ARR growth, underscoring the strength of our land-and-expand model and the increasing stickiness of our platform in enterprise accounts. For Q3 FY2024, we finished the quarter with total ARR of $452 million, representing 28% year-over-year growth from $353 million in Q3 FY2023, and 6% quarter-over-quarter growth from $426 million at the end of Q2 FY2024.

This performance outperformed our guidance and keeps us at the high end of the SaaS growth spectrum amid macro headwinds like elevated interest rates and cautious IT spending, similar to what Snowflake and Datadog have noted recently. Year-over-year, growth came from new ACV adds contributing about 45%, or $44 million incrementally, with 40 net new customers over $1 million ACV, up 20% year-over-year, including deals displacing legacy tools from IBM and Broadcom. Our AI-native workflow orchestration module enabled 40% faster deployments versus competitors like GitLab or Harness.

Net expansion drove 50% of growth, or $48 million, with dollar-based net retention at 118%, reflecting multi-product adoption where 70% of top 100 customers use three or more modules, including our Predictive Analytics Engine with OpenAI integrations. Gross revenue retention was 96%, aided by our Expansion Accelerator Program using ML for early upsell identification. Excluding FX drag of 1 point, organic growth was 29%, outpacing ServiceNow's CRPO growth.

Quarter-over-quarter, the 6% add of $26 million was balanced: $12 million from new business like a multi-year deal with an e-commerce platform reducing MTTR by 55%; $13 million from expansions, especially enterprise at 8% QoQ via GenAI Copilot with 85% adoption; and $1 million net from retention.

Geographically, North America at 78% of ARR or $352 million grew 30% YoY via AWS co-sell driving 20% of new logos. EMEA at 15% or $68 million accelerated to 38% YoY with GDPR features in UK fintech and German manufacturing. APAC at 7% or $32 million grew 22% YoY, offset by China but strong in India and Japan with Snowflake integrations. By segment, enterprise over $1M ARR at $295 million up 35% YoY and 62% of total; mid-market $125 million up 25%; SMB $32 million up 15%.

Our Kubernetes-native architecture delivers 99.99% uptime, with ForgeAI Suite cited in 40% of expansions showing 3-5x faster feature velocity. We're focused on Rule of 40 at 48, with CAC payback at 14 months and RPO up 33% to $620 million. We see 30%+ growth into FY2025 from AI tailwinds and $50 billion TAM.

Good afternoon, everyone. Moving on to gross margin, which remains a cornerstone of our financial health here at CloudForge, where we deliver our flagship SaaS platform for enterprise workflow automation—think of us as the next evolution of tools like Slack Enterprise Grid or Asana, but with deep AI-driven insights and zero-trust security baked in.

For Q3 FY2024, our GAAP gross margin came in at 78.5%, up 130 basis points sequentially from 77.2% in Q2 and 240 basis points year-over-year from 76.1% in Q3 FY2023. On a non-GAAP basis, excluding stock-based compensation and amortization, we hit 79.8%, reflecting operational leverage. For the full year to date, GAAP gross margin is 78.2%, a 290 basis point improvement from last year, driven by multi-tenant cloud scalability.

With Q3 revenue of $115 million up 28% year-over-year, this expansion comes from disciplined cost management. First, scale efficiencies in cloud infrastructure: average revenue per compute instance down 15% YoY via 40% higher tenant density on Kubernetes clusters. As ARR scaled, fixed costs amortized well; we migrated 65% of legacy workloads to ForgeCore v2.0 using spot instances, cutting COGS per seat 8-10%.

Second, product mix shift: NRR of 118% drove upsells to higher-margin ForgeAI analytics, now at 42% of customers versus 28% last year, with margins over 85%. On-prem licenses down to under 2% of revenue.

Third, support optimization: GenAI chatbots cut agent hours 25% at 98.5% CSAT. In EMEA, up 35% YoY to $30 million revenue, localized support in Dublin and Frankfurt reduced contractors 18%. APAC up 42% to $15 million benefited from Singapore data center, improving local margins to 77%.

Headwinds included 40 basis points from USD strength on 28% non-USD revenue, and GPU investments for ForgeAI amid Nvidia shortages like at Snowflake. These are front-loaded. Forward, targeting 79-80% non-GAAP by FY2025 via hyperscaler discounts, marketplace integrations like Okta and ServiceNow at 90%+ margins, and serverless focus ahead of 25% AI spend CAGR per Gartner. This boosts our Rule of 50 to 58, enabling sales investments like Salesforce in 2022.

Thank you, Sarah. Now, turning to sales efficiency, which remains a cornerstone of our high-growth SaaS model here at CloudForge. Sales efficiency optimizes the revenue flywheel—shortening cycles, boosting conversions, and driving down CAC while accelerating payback. Our sales efficiency score is 1.4x quarterly, above 1.0x top-quartile per Bessemer, with magic number 1.25x.

Median sales cycle for new ACV deals was 92 days in Q3, 15% better than 108 days last year and 8% from Q1's 100 days, outperforming industry 84-120 days per OpenView via PLG like Snowflake. Self-serve/SMB at 42% of new ARR closed in 45 days via freemium; mid-market 105 days with bottoms-up; enterprise 145 days shortened 22% YoY via AWS, Salesforce integrations.

Americas at 85 days for AI workflow in fintech/e-commerce; EMEA 110 days improving via Frankfurt DC; APAC 120 days with Tencent pilots to cut 20-25 days. Our Sales Copilot with GPT-4 automates 40% discovery, qualifying 2.5x faster; Gong battlecards provide competitive intel vs Adobe/Oracle.

Conversion rates: lead-to-customer 8.2% up from 6.9% YoY, SQL-to-won 37% up from 32%, top decile per benchmarks. Funnel: MQL-SQL 28% via inbound SEO; SQL-opp 72% with ABM; opp-close 37% via MEDDPICC and quick POCs like Outreach. Q3 at 8.2%, July pipeline 9%. CAC down 14% to $28k per ACV dollar, LTV/CAC 5.8x, payback 14 months. Q4 targets under 90 days, 9.5% conversion via PLG and 6sense.

Thank you, Sarah. Moving now to our free cash flow performance, a hallmark of CloudForge's maturing SaaS model. For Q3, we generated $70 million in free cash flow, up 60% year-over-year, or 61% of revenue. Year-to-date, $210 million, toward full-year $285 million guidance, 28% of revenue up 500 bps, ahead of 25-30% target.

Operating cash flow $78 million from profitability and working capital. CapEx $8 million or 7% of revenue for AI infra on AWS. Revenue growth and leverage: ARR up 28% to $452 million, NRR 118%, non-GAAP op margin 32% up from 25%, Rule of 40 at 68. Cash conversion 112% of EBITDA, DSO 52 days via Stripe, deferred revenue up 28% to $180 million.

GTM discipline: CAC payback 11 months via PLG driving 40% new ARR like HubSpot. Gross margins 78% via AWS savings 15%. North America 60% revenue +25%; EMEA +45% with DAX wins; APAC +30%. $100 million buybacks, $450 million cash, no debt. FY2025 guide $380-410 million FCF. Challenges offset by land-and-expand, 98% retention.

Before guidance, our key assumptions for FY2025 revenue $1.25-1.28 billion, 24-27% growth midpoint, adjusted op income $285-295 million at 23% margin. Grounded in $2.1 billion RPO up 32%, current RPO +28%.

Customer metrics: NRR 118-120%, enterprise upsell 25-30%, ACV $450-500k, 3.2-year deals, mid/SMB ACV +8-10%, 12-14k net adds, <5% churn. Macro: 2-2.5% US GDP, no recession, 10-15% longer cycles offset by 85% POC wins, 3-5% pricing.

Product: AI suite 15-20% bookings, 40% attach, DAUs +35%; ForgeEdge low-code rollout 25% penetration. 90%+ margins offset $50 million R&D. Regions: Americas 25-28% via hyperscalers; EMEA 30% DACH; APAC 35% Japan/Australia. GTM: S&M 45% revenue, 1.6-1.8x payback, Rule of 60 at 65, $150 million repurchases. Conservative H2 weighting, 10% buffer. Risks: economy, competition like Microsoft Viva/Notion, AI regs; but $850 million cash, 130 Rule of 40.

Thanks, Sarah. Before Q&A, some color on Q4 outlook, ARR our north star for SaaS durability in workflow automation. Q3 closed $452 million, +28% YoY +6% QoQ from $28 million net adds: $12 million from 15 enterprise logos like Fortune 500 in financials/healthcare akin to Workday/ServiceNow; $16 million expansions at 118% NRR. Churn <0.8%.

Q4 guide $475-482 million, 5-6.5% sequential, 26-28% YoY, conservative for macro/elongated Europe cycles. New ACV $30-34 million focused mid-market 35% YoY now 22% ARR; enterprise 65% YoY prudent on closes. NRR 116-119% via ForgeAI at 60% attach, 40% faster deployments like UiPath. Churn sub-1%, insulated by contracts.

Regions: NA 6-7% via AWS $8 million pipeline, Azure $15 million; EMEA 4-5% Germany SAP up 45%; APAC 8-10% Japan/Singapore DC. Embeds $10 million RPO growth, $1.2 billion total +32% YoY; $5 million headwind legacy. Q4 GA Federated Learning privacy AI, Salesforce/Oracle integrations $20 million pipeline. Risks FX/competition like Appian; 1.8x Rule of 40, FY24 $1.85 billion midpoint.

We are maintaining strong FY24 outlook.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lena Novak for a technology update.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you, Mike. This quarter, we made significant progress in advancing our AI capabilities and further integrating them into our core platform. We are seeing strong adoption of our new AI-powered features, which are driving increased user engagement and improved customer outcomes. We've also focused on enhancing our platform's security and scalability to meet the growing demands of our enterprise customers, with 99.99% uptime and sub-50ms latency at scale.

And now Taylor Kim will provide an update on the product roadmap.

Taylor Kim:
Thank you, Lena. We have been focusing on the user experience of our products and are excited to announce the general availability of ApexAI Gen3, our next-gen conversational AI engine, along with ApexFlow 2.0 low-code platform and ApexVertical Packs. These significantly improve workflow orchestration, personalization, and vertical-specific automation. Adoption is strong at 42% for AI suite, driving 22% MAU growth and 118% NRR, with 65% customers activating three+ features.

ApexAI Gen3 with Anthropic Claude 3.5 and our 175B model delivers 40% faster responses, 35% better accuracy: zero-shot personalization up 28% CSAT; multimodal voice/video; agentic workflows cutting agent involvement 52%. New AICU pricing added $14 million ARR from 450 adopters, 72% upgrading ARPU +$4,200. NA 55%, APAC +140% localized.

ApexFlow 2.0 3x faster builds, 500 connectors Snowflake/ServiceNow; predictive optimization 31% cost cuts; edge WebAssembly 45% latency drop; zero-trust security SOC2/ISO. MAUs +38% QoQ, 22% marketplace apps, +14% DBNER. EMEA 28% new logos GDPR.

Vertical packs: BFSI FraudShield 97% precision; healthcare FHIR +26% adherence; retail 19% basket lifts. APAC ARR +62% Singapore; EMEA +34% UK. Q1 2025 betas Gen4 agents, multi-cloud Bedrock/Vertex. K-factor 1.3, 95% retention positions us in $13 trillion AI value.

This aligns with our product strategy.

Riley Thompson:
Thank you, Taylor. This quarter our focus was on increasing our brand awareness and lead generation through targeted digital campaigns and strategic partnerships. We saw a 35% increase in website traffic and a 42% increase in qualified leads, demonstrating the effectiveness of our marketing initiatives, particularly inbound SEO and ABM for high-intent workflow AI searches.

Now, I'll turn the call back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith:
Hi, good afternoon. Can you discuss the impact of ForgeAI on your overall growth, what kind of attach rates are you seeing, how it compares to your initial expectations, and what's the competitive landscape like?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Ben. ForgeAI has been transformative for growth, contributing 25% of Q3 expansions and 40% of new logos, accelerating ARR adds by $16 million. Attach rates are north of 60% in existing seats and 40% on new deals, driving NRR to 118%. This exceeded our expectations by 15% in adoption velocity, with ROI showing 40% faster deployments. Competitively, we're gaining share from UiPath and Appian in process mining, with superior privacy via Federated Learning and hyperscaler integrations giving us an edge in regulated verticals.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Emily Chen:
What are your plans for international expansion, specifically in the APAC region, what are your key target markets, and what are your expected ROI from these investments?

Sarah Chen:
Great question, Emily. International expansion is a priority, with APAC targeted for 8-10% sequential ARR growth in Q4. Plans include Singapore DC go-live reducing latency for trading clients, Mandarin playbooks, and Tencent co-sell. Key markets: Japan enterprises, India mid-market telco/retail, Australia logistics. Expected ROI is 3x within 18 months via land-and-expand, mirroring our EMEA ramp, with $15 million pipeline acceleration already.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan.

David Lee:
How are you managing churn in the current economic environment, what's the trend you are seeing in NRR, what's your strategies to improve customer retention, and what's the impact of pricing changes on churn?

Mike Patel:
Thanks, David. Churn management is proactive: gross dollar churn under 0.8%, best-in-class, no bankruptcy impact due to multi-year contracts in compliance verticals. NRR steady at 118%, trending 116-119% Q4. Strategies include Expansion Accelerator with ML usage analytics, GenAI support reducing tickets 25%, and 95%+ renewals. Pricing true-ups 3-5% and usage tiers have neutral to positive impact, boosting ARPU without churn uptick, as seen in mid-market expansions.

Operator:
Thank you. I'm showing no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the call back over to Sarah Chen for closing remarks.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain committed to delivering strong results for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again on our next earnings call.

Operator:
Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
